scenes.title: Composite Index
scenes.narration: A composite index covers several columns at once, and the order of those columns changes everything about how it can be used.

scenes.title: The core idea
bullets: One index built on two or more columns in a fixed order
The index is sorted by the first column, then the second, and so on
Column order is a design decision, not a detail
scenes.narration: A composite index is a single index built on two or more columns in a fixed order. Its entries are sorted by the first column, then within that by the second, and so on down the list. That ordering means the column sequence is a real design decision rather than an afterthought.

scenes.title: Create a composite index
scenes.narration: This index orders rows first by customer_id and then by order_date. The query filters on customer_id and then order_date, matching the index from its leading column onward. So the engine can seek to the right customer and then scan the date range within that customer efficiently.

scenes.title: The leftmost-prefix rule
steps: Filtering on customer_id alone uses the index
Filtering on customer_id and order_date uses it fully
Filtering on order_date alone cannot use it
A leading prefix must be present to seek
scenes.narration: The leftmost-prefix rule governs when the index helps. Filtering on customer_id alone works, and filtering on both columns works even better. But filtering on order_date alone cannot use this index, because a leading prefix must be present for the engine to seek into it.

scenes.title: Ordering the columns

left.title: Good order
points: Most selective leading column when equal

right.title: Poor order
points: Forces a scan instead of a seek

scenes.narration: A good composite index puts equality columns first and the range column last, and favors the most selective column when choices are otherwise equal. A poor order places a range column ahead of an equality column, which forces a scan rather than a tight seek, or leads with a column your queries seldom filter on by itself.

scenes.text: Order composite index columns by how queries filter: equality first, range last, and remember a query must match a leading prefix to benefit.
scenes.narration: Order the columns of a composite index by how your queries actually filter, putting equality columns first and range columns last, and remember that a query only benefits when it matches a leading prefix.
